chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
My father bought a piece of land and stipulated upon its owner that he would give him silver (dirhams), every dinar for ten dirhams.
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on stipulating specific currency for payment in a land sale contract in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the permissibility of stipulating specific currency types and exchange rates in land transactions, reflecting the practical commercial jurisprudence of the Ahl al-Bayt. It underscores the flexibility in Islamic contract law (Fiqh al-Mu'amalat) to accommodate local economic conditions while ensuring fairness in monetary exchange. The narration serves as a precedent for modern financial contracts involving currency specifications and fixed exchange mechanisms.
